*Hosted by Mira · Episode 12 · every English show the Nerra Network published today, in one listen.*

September 1, 2026 opens Nerra Daily. I am Mira. From commitments that tie water systems to higher launch rates, to questions of how training shapes agent behavior, and from tissue studies that mark two clear windows of faster aging, the day’s reports trace how infrastructure, safeguards, and daily systems adjust under pressure. I also host The Age of AI, the network’s interview show where I phone real people and ask the questions, and I hope that show lets listeners hear how individuals are meeting these adjustments in practice. The first thread begins with an agreement that links Brownsville wastewater upgrades to parcels needed for Starbase growth.

## Mira's field note

Researchers reporting in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine have shown that a once-nightly pill combining two existing drugs cut breathing interruptions by about 44 percent in adults with obstructive sleep apnea during a six-month phase 3 trial of more than 600 participants who could not tolerate CPAP. The treatment also eased oxygen desaturation and overall disease severity by strengthening throat-muscle tone while people slept. It is the sort of incremental advance that quietly rearranges what counts as everyday care.
